words.enDefinition: How individuals or households choose, acquire, and respond to products or services for personal use.

examples.en: The module introduces consumer buying behavior through fictional accounts of students choosing supplies for shared studio work.
examples.zh: 课程单元通过虚构学生选择共用工作室用品的记述，介绍「消费者购买行为」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares consumer buying behavior for ordinary supplies with decisions about longer-lasting items in the same category.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较购买普通用品和同类耐用品时的「消费者购买行为」。

words.enDefinition: A framework describing stages such as recognising a need, exploring options, choosing, and evaluating the outcome.

examples.en: The diagram illustrates the consumer decision process through a fictional purchase of a reusable lunch container.
examples.zh: 示意图用虚构的可重复使用餐盒购买案例说明「消费者决策过程」。

examples.en: Our textbook notes that the consumer decision process may include fewer steps for familiar routine purchases.
examples.zh: 教材指出，购买熟悉的日常用品时，「消费者决策过程」可能包含较少步骤。

collocations: stages of the consumer decision process
model of the consumer decision process

words.enDefinition: In the consumer decision process, noticing a difference between one's current situation and a desired one.

examples.en: The fictional story illustrates need recognition when the student notices their old folder no longer closes properly.
examples.zh: 虚构故事以一名学生发现旧文件夹盖不紧的时点，说明「需求识别」。

examples.en: Our class discusses need recognition before the character begins comparing containers for the new university studio.
examples.zh: 我们在角色开始为大学新工作室比较容器以前，讨论「需求识别」这一阶段。

words.zhGloss: 触发需求识别的内部刺激
words.enDefinition: A cue originating within the consumer, such as a bodily sensation or personal goal, that makes a need salient.
acceptedZhAnswers: 触发需求识别的内部刺激

examples.en: The case describes hunger as an internal stimulus for need recognition before the fictional shopper considers a snack.
examples.zh: 案例将虚构购物者考虑买零食前感到饥饿，描述为一种「触发需求识别的内部刺激」。

examples.en: Our worksheet identifies an internal stimulus for need recognition in one of its two fictional examples.
examples.zh: 练习单在两个虚构示例之一中指出了一项「触发需求识别的内部刺激」。

collocations: identify an internal stimulus for need recognition
example of an internal stimulus for need recognition
classify an internal stimulus for need recognition

words.zhGloss: 触发需求识别的外部刺激
words.enDefinition: An environmental or social cue that draws a consumer's attention to a possible unmet need.
acceptedZhAnswers: 触发需求识别的外部刺激

examples.en: The fictional timetable change represents an external stimulus for need recognition when students consider buying earlier meals.
examples.zh: 虚构课表变动促使学生考虑早点买饭，属于一种「触发需求识别的外部刺激」。

examples.en: The class identifies an external stimulus for need recognition in the fictional diary entry about a shared project.
examples.zh: 全班在关于共同项目的虚构日记里，找出一种「触发需求识别的外部刺激」。

collocations: identify an external stimulus for need recognition
example of an external stimulus for need recognition
classify an external stimulus for need recognition

words.enDefinition: The stage or activity of seeking information relevant to a possible purchase.

examples.en: The fictional account describes information search in buying as the student examines guides before choosing an art folder.
examples.zh: 虚构记述通过学生先查资料再选美术文件夹的一幕，描述「购买时的信息搜寻」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares information search in buying a familiar notebook and in choosing an unfamiliar tool.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较购买熟悉笔记本和挑选不熟悉工具时的「购买时的信息搜寻」。

collocations: extent of information search in buying
stage of information search in buying

words.enDefinition: Retrieving relevant knowledge or past experiences from memory when making a consumer decision.

examples.en: The worksheet labels remembering past notebook purchases as internal information search in its fictional shopping vignette.
examples.zh: 练习单把虚构购物情境中回忆以往笔记本购买经历的行为标记为「内部信息搜寻」。

examples.en: Our seminar considers how internal information search may draw on experience from a previous university project.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论「内部信息搜寻」可能怎样利用过去大学项目中的经验。

collocations: internal information search before a purchase

words.enDefinition: Looking beyond memory to other people, publicly available material, or product information to inform a consumer decision.

examples.en: The fictional shopper consults a product guide during external information search for an unfamiliar type of folder.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者挑选不熟悉的文件夹时查看产品指南，进行了「外部信息搜寻」。

examples.en: Our reading compares external information search in two fictional purchasing decisions with different levels of familiarity.
examples.zh: 读物比较两项熟悉程度不同的虚构购买决策中的「外部信息搜寻」。

words.enDefinition: The stage in which consumers compare possible options using relevant characteristics or standards.

examples.en: The class illustrates evaluation of alternatives by comparing size, weight, and durability across three fictional notebooks.
examples.zh: 课堂通过比较三种虚构笔记本的尺寸、重量和耐用性来说明「备选方案评估」。

examples.en: Our worksheet places evaluation of alternatives between looking up information and making a final purchase choice.
examples.zh: 练习单把「备选方案评估」放在查询信息和作出最终购买选择之间。

words.enDefinition: The attributes or standards a consumer uses to compare possible purchases.

examples.en: The fictional shopper lists durability and space as consumer evaluative criteria for choosing a studio storage box.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者选工作室储物盒时，将耐用性和空间列为「消费者的评估标准」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares consumer evaluative criteria across two fictional buyers with different uses for the same item.
examples.zh: 研讨课对比两名对同一物品用途不同的虚构买家的「消费者的评估标准」。

words.enDefinition: The subset of available options a consumer actively considers for a particular choice.

examples.en: The fictional shopper narrows the consideration set to two pencil cases before examining how each one closes.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者把「认真考虑的备选集合」缩小到两个笔袋，然后查看各自的闭合方式。

examples.en: Our class compares the consideration set with the longer list of items available in the sample catalogue.
examples.zh: 全班把「认真考虑的备选集合」与样本目录中较长的可选物品列表作比较。

words.zhGloss: 消费者已知的选项集合
words.enDefinition: The options in a category that a consumer knows exist, whether or not they would consider buying them.
acceptedZhAnswers: 消费者已知的选项集合

examples.en: The fictional diagram places the awareness set above a smaller list of options the student would seriously consider.
examples.zh: 虚构示意图把「消费者已知的选项集合」列在学生会认真考虑的较短清单上方。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which products are in the awareness set even though several never reach active consideration.
examples.zh: 练习单询问哪些产品属于「消费者已知的选项集合」，尽管有几个从未进入实际考虑范围。

words.zhGloss: 消费者无明显倾向的选项集合
words.enDefinition: Known alternatives about which a consumer is indifferent or has no definite opinion.
acceptedZhAnswers: 消费者无明显倾向的选项集合

examples.en: In the fictional example, several known notebooks fall into the inert set because the student feels indifferent.
examples.zh: 在虚构示例中，学生对几种已知笔记本态度中立，因此它们属于「消费者无明显倾向的选项集合」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes the inert set from the options the fictional shopper rules out for a stated reason.
examples.zh: 练习单把「消费者无明显倾向的选项集合」与虚构购物者因明确理由排除的选项区分开来。

collocations: include an option in the inert set

words.zhGloss: 消费者排除的选项集合
words.enDefinition: Known alternatives a consumer rejects or regards as unacceptable for the purchase at hand.
acceptedZhAnswers: 消费者排除的选项集合

examples.en: The fictional shopper places oversized cases in the inept set because they cannot fit the assigned locker.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者把过大的箱盒列入「消费者排除的选项集合」，因为放不进分配的储物柜。

examples.en: Our class sorts known options into active choices and the inept set in a fictional product comparison.
examples.zh: 全班在虚构产品比较中，把已知选项分为积极考虑的选项和「消费者排除的选项集合」。

collocations: classify an option in the inept set

words.enDefinition: A way of evaluating options that allows strengths on one attribute to compensate for weaknesses on another.

examples.en: The fictional comparison illustrates a compensatory decision rule when lower weight offsets reduced storage space for one buyer.
examples.zh: 虚构比较中，对于一位买家而言，重量更轻弥补了收纳空间变小，体现「补偿性决策规则」。

examples.en: Our textbook uses a compensatory decision rule to explain how two attributes can contribute to the overall judgement.
examples.zh: 教材用「补偿性决策规则」说明两项属性如何共同影响总体判断。

words.enDefinition: An evaluation rule under which weakness on one key attribute cannot always be offset by strengths on other attributes.

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates a noncompensatory decision rule when the fictional buyer rejects every item too large for storage.
examples.zh: 练习单用虚构买家拒绝所有放不进储物空间的物品这一例子，说明「非补偿性决策规则」。

examples.en: Our class discussed how a noncompensatory decision rule differs from adding all the fictional product scores together.
examples.zh: 全班讨论「非补偿性决策规则」与把虚构产品的所有评分相加有何区别。

words.zhGloss: 各项均须达标的决策规则
words.enDefinition: A rule accepting an option only if it meets minimum standards on every selected attribute.
acceptedZhAnswers: 各项均须达标的决策规则

examples.en: The fictional shopper follows a conjunctive decision rule by keeping only boxes that meet both size requirements.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者采用「各项均须达标的决策规则」，只保留符合两个尺寸要求的盒子。

examples.en: Our worksheet uses a conjunctive decision rule to explain why one missed requirement eliminates an otherwise acceptable choice.
examples.zh: 练习单用「各项均须达标的决策规则」说明，为什么缺一项要求就会排除原本可以接受的选项。

collocations: minimum standards in a conjunctive decision rule

words.zhGloss: 任一项达标即可的决策规则
words.enDefinition: A rule accepting an option if it reaches a specified threshold on at least one selected attribute.
acceptedZhAnswers: 任一项达标即可的决策规则

examples.en: The fictional buyer follows a disjunctive decision rule by accepting bags that excel in size or durability.
examples.zh: 虚构买家按照「任一项达标即可的决策规则」，只要包的尺寸或耐用性有一个表现突出就接受。

examples.en: Our tutor demonstrates a disjunctive decision rule using two independent ways for a fictional option to qualify.
examples.zh: 老师用虚构选项的两条独立达标途径演示「任一项达标即可的决策规则」。

collocations: example of a disjunctive decision rule

words.zhGloss: 按属性优先次序选择的规则
words.enDefinition: A rule choosing by the most important attribute first and using less important attributes to break ties.
acceptedZhAnswers: 按属性优先次序选择的规则

examples.en: The fictional shopper uses a lexicographic decision rule by considering weight only when two options fit equally.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者采用「按属性优先次序选择的规则」，只有两个选项同样合适时才考虑重量。

examples.en: Our class applied a lexicographic decision rule to a table of fictional lunch containers with duplicate scores.
examples.zh: 全班用「按属性优先次序选择的规则」处理一张含相同评分的虚构餐盒表。

words.enDefinition: The stage in a consumer decision model when the person decides whether, what, or how to buy.

examples.en: Our diagram labels the purchase decision stage after the fictional shopper has compared the remaining products.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者比较完剩余产品后，示意图标出接下来的「购买决策阶段」。

examples.en: The worksheet asks which part of the story belongs to the purchase decision stage in the model.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，故事的哪一部分属于模型中的「购买决策阶段」。

collocations: decisions at the purchase decision stage
factors at the purchase decision stage

words.enDefinition: A consumer's assessment of a purchase after acquiring or using the product or service.

examples.en: The case illustrates postpurchase evaluation when a fictional student reflects on how the notebook performed during class.
examples.zh: 案例通过虚构学生回顾笔记本在上课时的使用表现来说明「购后评价」。

examples.en: Our discussion separates postpurchase evaluation from the information the fictional shopper collected before choosing the item.
examples.zh: 讨论将「购后评价」与虚构购物者选择该物品前收集的信息区分开来。

words.enDefinition: How personally relevant or important a product or buying decision feels to a consumer in context.

examples.en: The tutor introduces consumer involvement through two fictional shoppers who assign very different importance to the purchase.
examples.zh: 老师借两名对这次购买重视程度迥异的虚构购物者介绍「消费者涉入度」。

examples.en: Our worksheet describes consumer involvement separately from how many alternatives are actually available in the sample catalogue.
examples.zh: 练习单对「消费者涉入度」单独作了描述，与样本目录中实际有多少选项分开。

words.enDefinition: A personally important purchase for which the consumer may devote substantial care or effort to the decision.

examples.en: The fictional student treats a long-lasting work chair as a high-involvement purchase and compares alternatives across several weeks.
examples.zh: 虚构学生把一把能长期使用的工作椅当成「高涉入购买」，用了几周比较备选项。

examples.en: Our class asks why the same item can be a high-involvement purchase for one buyer but not another.
examples.zh: 全班讨论同一物品为何对一个买家属于「高涉入购买」，对另一个买家却未必。

words.enDefinition: A purchase experienced as relatively unimportant, often involving limited attention or effort in choosing.

examples.en: The textbook presents buying familiar binder clips as a low-involvement purchase in its fictional stationery example.
examples.zh: 教材在虚构文具示例中，把购买熟悉的长尾夹作为「低涉入购买」。

examples.en: Our discussion compares a low-involvement purchase with a choice that the fictional shopper thinks about for several days.
examples.zh: 讨论将一项「低涉入购买」与让虚构购物者考虑好几天的选择作对比。

words.enDefinition: In a consumer behaviour framework, a pattern of high involvement and perceived differences between alternatives.

examples.en: The worksheet describes complex buying behavior when a fictional shopper compares meaningfully different options for a long-term purchase.
examples.zh: 练习单以虚构购物者为一项长期购买对比存在实质差异的选项为例，说明「复杂购买行为」。

examples.en: Our seminar identifies complex buying behavior by checking both purchase importance and the perceived differences in the example.
examples.zh: 研讨课核看示例的购买重要性和感知差异，以辨认「复杂购买行为」。

words.zhGloss: 减少失调感的购买行为
words.enDefinition: In a marketing framework, high-involvement buying when the consumer sees little difference among available alternatives and may later seek reassurance.
acceptedZhAnswers: 减少失调感的购买行为

examples.en: The case compares dissonance-reducing buying behavior with another fictional purchase involving several clearly different alternatives.
examples.zh: 案例把「减少失调感的购买行为」与另一项有几个明显不同备选项的虚构购买相比较。

examples.en: Our worksheet links dissonance-reducing buying behavior to a fictional choice the student considers important despite similar alternatives.
examples.zh: 练习单将「减少失调感的购买行为」与虚构学生尽管面对相似备选项、仍认为很重要的选择联系起来。

words.enDefinition: Routine buying with little active decision effort, especially when alternatives are seen as similar.

examples.en: The chapter illustrates habitual buying behavior through repeat purchases of a familiar item in a fictional household.
examples.zh: 教材用一个虚构家庭反复购买一件熟悉物品的情形说明「习惯性购买行为」。

examples.en: Our study guide distinguishes habitual buying behavior from a strong stated preference for one particular fictional product.
examples.zh: 学习指南把「习惯性购买行为」与明确强烈偏好某一款虚构产品区分开来。

words.zhGloss: 寻求多样性的购买行为
words.enDefinition: Switching among offerings for novelty or variety, typically in a relatively low-involvement purchase category.
acceptedZhAnswers: 寻求多样性的购买行为

examples.en: The fictional consumer chooses another biscuit flavour for a change, which illustrates variety-seeking buying behavior in class.
examples.zh: 虚构消费者为了换换口味另选一种饼干，课堂以此说明「寻求多样性的购买行为」。

examples.en: Our reading separates variety-seeking buying behavior from switching products because a previous purchase was disappointing.
examples.zh: 读物把「寻求多样性的购买行为」与因先前购买令人失望而换产品的行为区分开来。

words.enDefinition: A choice made in the setting where a purchase occurs, including one made after arriving with an earlier plan.

examples.en: The fictional shopper makes a point-of-purchase decision after seeing the two notebook sizes in the campus shop.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者在校园商店看到两种尺寸的笔记本后，作出一项「购买现场作出的决策」。

examples.en: Our case distinguishes a point-of-purchase decision about colour from the earlier plan to buy a folder.
examples.zh: 案例区分选择颜色这一项「购买现场作出的决策」和先前购买文件夹的计划。

words.zhGloss: 有限型消费者问题解决
words.enDefinition: A purchase approach using some additional information or comparison without undertaking extensive evaluation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 有限型消费者问题解决

examples.en: The class uses limited consumer problem solving to describe a fictional buyer who checks two unfamiliar options briefly.
examples.zh: 全班用「有限型消费者问题解决」描述一位简单查看两个陌生选项的虚构买家。

examples.en: Our worksheet places limited consumer problem solving between routine responding and a much more detailed buying process.
examples.zh: 练习单把「有限型消费者问题解决」放在常规反应和详细得多的购买过程之间。

collocations: engage in limited consumer problem solving
example of limited consumer problem solving

words.zhGloss: 广泛型消费者问题解决
words.enDefinition: A purchase approach involving substantial information search and detailed evaluation of alternatives.
acceptedZhAnswers: 广泛型消费者问题解决

examples.en: The worksheet describes extended consumer problem solving when the fictional student compares several unfamiliar models in detail.
examples.zh: 练习单用虚构学生详细比较几个不熟悉型号的例子来说明「广泛型消费者问题解决」。

examples.en: Our tutor asks whether weeks of information search and evaluation amount to extended consumer problem solving here.
examples.zh: 老师讨论，本例持续数周的信息搜寻和评估是否构成「广泛型消费者问题解决」。

collocations: engage in extended consumer problem solving
example of extended consumer problem solving
demands of extended consumer problem solving

words.enDefinition: The person who first raises the idea or need for a particular purchase.

examples.en: The fictional household's purchase initiator notices that their shared storage supplies are running low before the discussion.
examples.zh: 虚构家庭的「购买发起者」在讨论前注意到共用收纳用品快用完了。

examples.en: Our role chart lists the purchase initiator separately from the character who will actually buy the item.
examples.zh: 角色表将「购买发起者」与实际购买物品的角色分开列出。

words.enDefinition: Someone whose advice or preferences help shape a purchase decision without necessarily making it.

examples.en: The casebook calls the fictional studio tutor a purchase influencer because their advice shaped the student's choice.
examples.zh: 案例教材将虚构工作室老师称为「购买影响者」，因为老师的意见影响了学生的选择。

examples.en: Our classroom chart separates the purchase influencer from the fictional buyer responsible for paying for the item.
examples.zh: 课堂图表把「购买影响者」与负责付款的虚构买家区分开来。

words.enDefinition: The person with the deciding say about whether or what to buy in a shared purchase.

examples.en: The study group identifies the purchase decision maker in the fictional household by reading the dialogue carefully.
examples.zh: 学习小组仔细阅读对话，辨认虚构家庭中的「购买决策者」。

examples.en: Our role map shows the purchase decision maker as one character and the product user as another.
examples.zh: 角色图显示，一名角色是「购买决策者」，另一名角色是产品使用者。

collocations: role of a purchase decision maker
authority of a purchase decision maker

words.enDefinition: An internal reason or drive behind a consumer's pursuit of a purchasing or consumption goal.

examples.en: The casebook compares consumer motivation across fictional students choosing the same kitchen item for different reasons.
examples.zh: 案例教材比较几名因不同原因挑选同一厨具的虚构学生的「消费者动机」。

examples.en: Our seminar discusses consumer motivation after reading several accounts of why the fictional shoppers began searching.
examples.zh: 研讨课阅读了几段讲述虚构购物者为什么开始搜寻的记述，然后讨论「消费者动机」。

words.enDefinition: A practical need that a product or service can meet by performing a useful function.

examples.en: The fictional student describes carrying papers without folding them as a functional need for the new folder.
examples.zh: 虚构学生把不用折叠就能携带纸张描述为对新文件夹的「功能性需求」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes the functional need for a container from the shopper's preference for a particular colour.
examples.zh: 练习单区分了对容器的「功能性需求」和购物者对特定颜色的偏好。

words.enDefinition: An incentive to shop or consume for enjoyment, sensory pleasure, or the experience itself.

examples.en: The seminar illustrates hedonic motivation through a fictional shopper who browses craft supplies simply for enjoyment.
examples.zh: 研讨课用虚构购物者单纯为了乐趣浏览手工用品的一幕说明「享乐动机」。

examples.en: Our worksheet identifies hedonic motivation in a fictional account of someone choosing a product for its enjoyable texture.
examples.zh: 练习单在虚构人物因产品质地带来愉悦而作选择的记述中辨认出「享乐动机」。

words.enDefinition: An incentive to shop or consume to accomplish a practical task or achieve an instrumental benefit.

examples.en: The fictional shopper's main reason for buying a folder is keeping papers organised, which illustrates utilitarian motivation.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者购买文件夹的主要目的是理好纸张，体现了「实用动机」。

examples.en: Our class contrasts utilitarian motivation in the first example with shopping for enjoyment in the second.
examples.zh: 全班把第一个例子的「实用动机」与第二个例子中享受购物乐趣作比较。

words.enDefinition: An outcome a consumer hopes to achieve through choosing or using a product or service.

examples.en: In the fictional vignette, the consumption goal is keeping drawing supplies organised during a shared studio session.
examples.zh: 在虚构材料中，「消费目标」是在共有工作室活动中将绘画用品摆放整齐。

examples.en: Our worksheet identifies the consumption goal before assessing which characteristics of the products would support it.
examples.zh: 练习单先找出「消费目标」，再评估产品的哪些特点有助于实现它。

collocations: product associated with a consumption goal

words.enDefinition: A factor that motivates or strongly influences a consumer's decision to make a purchase.

examples.en: The classroom survey identifies ease of storage as a purchase driver for a fictional group of buyers.
examples.zh: 课堂调查将易于存放列为一个虚构买家群体的「购买驱动因素」。

examples.en: Our summary explains how a purchase driver can differ depending on what students need from the product.
examples.zh: 摘要说明了「购买驱动因素」如何随学生对产品的需求而变化。

words.enDefinition: A factor that makes a consumer less likely or less able to complete a purchase.

examples.en: The class identifies limited storage space as a purchase barrier in the fictional household's product comparison.
examples.zh: 全班将有限的存放空间认定为虚构家庭比较产品时的一项「购买障碍」。

examples.en: Our sample report shows how a purchase barrier affected otherwise interested shoppers in the fictional survey.
examples.zh: 样本报告展示，某项「购买障碍」如何影响虚构调查中原本有兴趣的购物者。

words.enDefinition: The event or situation giving rise to a particular purchase.

examples.en: The example identifies the start of a new art class as the purchase occasion for replacement folders.
examples.zh: 示例将新美术课开课认定为更换文件夹的「购买场合」。

examples.en: Our survey summary distinguishes the purchase occasion from the later situation in which the product was used.
examples.zh: 调查摘要把「购买场合」和后来使用产品的情境区分开来。

words.enDefinition: A group a consumer uses as a point of comparison or as a source of norms or information.

examples.en: The fictional shopper treats a campus art club as a reference group when considering supplies for workshops.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者在考虑工作坊用品时，把校园美术社视为「参照群体」。

examples.en: Our seminar asks which reference group provides a point of comparison in the imaginary buyer's account.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，虚构买家的记述中哪一个「参照群体」提供了比较依据。

collocations: use a reference group for comparison

words.enDefinition: A group a person admires or would like to join or resemble.

examples.en: The casebook calls the fictional design society an aspirational reference group because the student hopes to join it.
examples.zh: 案例教材称虚构设计学会为「向往的参照群体」，因为学生希望加入它。

examples.en: Our worksheet separates an aspirational reference group from a group to which the fictional shopper already belongs.
examples.zh: 练习单将「向往的参照群体」与虚构购物者已经加入的群体区分开。

collocations: influence of an aspirational reference group
example of an aspirational reference group

words.zhGloss: 希望保持距离的参照群体
words.enDefinition: A group a person prefers not to resemble or be associated with.
acceptedZhAnswers: 希望保持距离的参照群体

examples.en: The seminar uses a fictional campus event to discuss what it means to have a dissociative reference group.
examples.zh: 研讨课借一场虚构校园活动，讨论拥有一个「希望保持距离的参照群体」意味着什么。

examples.en: The fictional shopper describes a dissociative reference group whose style they would prefer to avoid resembling.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者描述一个「希望保持距离的参照群体」，并表示不想自己的风格和这群人相似。

collocations: example of a dissociative reference group
avoid association with a dissociative reference group

words.enDefinition: The process of learning skills, norms, and habits involved in participating in consumer life.

examples.en: The casebook illustrates consumer socialization through a fictional student learning how a household compares everyday products.
examples.zh: 案例教材用虚构学生学习一个家庭如何比较日常商品的例子，说明「消费者社会化」。

examples.en: Our lecture considers how different social settings can contribute to consumer socialization in the classroom examples.
examples.zh: 讲座讨论，在课堂示例中，不同的社会环境如何参与「消费者社会化」。

words.enDefinition: Beliefs a consumer holds before buying about the performance or experience a product or service will provide.

examples.en: The fictional diary records prepurchase expectations about how much space the new container would provide during use.
examples.zh: 虚构日记记下了关于新容器使用时能提供多少空间的「购买前预期」。

examples.en: Our class compared prepurchase expectations with the experience described after several uses of the fictional product.
examples.zh: 我们把「购买前预期」与虚构产品用过几次之后所描述的体验作比较。

words.enDefinition: The consumer's assessment of what an option offers relative to its cost, effort, or other sacrifices.

examples.en: The class compares perceived value across two fictional folders with different prices and expected years of use.
examples.zh: 全班比较预计使用年限和价格不同的两个虚构文件夹的「感知价值」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes perceived value from the price recorded for the product in the sample catalogue.
examples.zh: 练习单把「感知价值」与样本目录所记载的产品价格区分开。

words.enDefinition: A consumer's judgement of the overall quality or excellence of an offering.

examples.en: The survey vignette compares perceived quality ratings from buyers using identical fictional products in different settings.
examples.zh: 调查材料比较了在不同情境下使用同样虚构产品的买家所给出的「感知质量」评分。

examples.en: Our class asks why perceived quality in the survey may differ from an independent assessment of durability.
examples.zh: 全班讨论调查中的「感知质量」为何可能与独立的耐用性评估不同。

words.enDefinition: The uncertainty and potential negative consequences a consumer associates with a possible purchase.

examples.en: The fictional shopper describes perceived risk as uncertainty about whether a storage box will fit the shelf.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者所说的「感知风险」，是无法确定储物盒能否放上架子。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares perceived risk across purchases involving similar prices but different consequences if the item disappoints.
examples.zh: 练习单比较了价格相近、但物品不尽如人意时后果不同的购买案例中的「感知风险」。

words.enDefinition: A consumer's perceived chance that an option will not work adequately or as expected.

examples.en: The case illustrates product performance risk when a fictional student doubts a folder will hold larger drawings.
examples.zh: 案例用虚构学生不确定文件夹能否装下较大画稿的一幕说明「性能风险」。

examples.en: Our survey summary separates product performance risk from concerns about how much the product costs in the example.
examples.zh: 调查摘要把「性能风险」与示例中对产品价格的顾虑区分开来。

words.enDefinition: The possibility, as perceived by a shopper, that a purchase will lead to a monetary loss or poor use of money.

examples.en: The vignette illustrates financial risk of a purchase when a fictional student anticipates needing a costly replacement.
examples.zh: 材料中的虚构学生预计需要再花不少钱换新，体现了「购买的财务风险」。

examples.en: Our class considers the financial risk of a purchase separately from uncertainty about how the product will work.
examples.zh: 全班把「购买的财务风险」与对产品能否正常发挥作用的疑虑分开考虑。

collocations: judge the financial risk of a purchase
perceived financial risk of a purchase
discuss the financial risk of a purchase

words.enDefinition: The perceived possibility that a buying choice may be judged negatively by people important to the consumer.

examples.en: The fictional student worries teammates will disapprove of the new supplies, illustrating social risk of a purchase.
examples.zh: 虚构学生担心队友不认可新买的用品，体现了「购买的社会风险」。

examples.en: Our casebook asks whether concern about teammates' opinions reflects social risk of a purchase in the story.
examples.zh: 案例教材询问，故事中对队友看法的担心是否反映了「购买的社会风险」。

collocations: assess the social risk of a purchase
perceived social risk of a purchase
concern about the social risk of a purchase

words.enDefinition: A consumer's perceived possibility of wasting time on a purchase or losing time if it goes wrong.

examples.en: The fictional comparison mentions time risk of a purchase if an unsuitable container has to be exchanged later.
examples.zh: 虚构比较提到，如果不合适的容器之后必须换货，就存在「购买中的时间风险」。

examples.en: Our seminar identifies the time risk of a purchase separately from the possible costs described by the shopper.
examples.zh: 研讨课将「购买中的时间风险」与购物者描述的潜在费用分别辨认。

collocations: assess the time risk of a purchase
discuss the time risk of a purchase
perceived time risk of a purchase

words.enDefinition: The weight or priority a consumer gives to a product characteristic when judging options.

examples.en: The fictional comparison shows attribute importance by ranking fit ahead of style for one intended use.
examples.zh: 虚构比较把适配程度排在样式前面，说明了特定用途下的「属性重要性」。

examples.en: Our survey chart compares attribute importance across fictional shoppers who plan to use the products in different ways.
examples.zh: 调查图表比较打算以不同方式使用产品的虚构购物者所看重的「属性重要性」。

words.enDefinition: A choice accepting less of one desirable characteristic to obtain more of another.

examples.en: The case describes an attribute trade-off when the fictional buyer accepts greater weight to get more storage space.
examples.zh: 案例用虚构买家为获得更多储存空间而接受较重产品的情形，描述「属性取舍」。

examples.en: Our tutor asks which attribute trade-off explains the buyer's preference for the fictional container with thicker walls.
examples.zh: 老师询问，买家偏爱厚壁虚构容器可由哪种「属性取舍」解释。

words.enDefinition: A consumer's stated or inferred plan or likelihood of buying a specific product or service.

examples.en: The fictional survey records purchase intention before the students compare it with the later number of actual purchases.
examples.zh: 虚构调查先记录「购买意向」，随后学生将其与后来的实际购买数量对照。

examples.en: Our teacher reminds us that purchase intention can reflect a plan formed before the shopper faces practical constraints.
examples.zh: 老师提醒我们，「购买意向」可能反映购物者遇到实际限制之前所作的计划。

words.enDefinition: Postponing a purchase decision while leaving open the possibility of buying later.

examples.en: The fictional diary illustrates purchase deferral when a shopper waits for more information before choosing a lamp.
examples.zh: 虚构日记以购物者等待了解更多信息再挑灯的一幕说明「推迟购买决定」。

examples.en: Our class discusses purchase deferral after reading why the fictional buyer planned to return the following week.
examples.zh: 全班读了虚构买家为什么计划下周再回来，然后讨论「推迟购买决定」。

words.enDefinition: How often a person or group buys a product or category during a defined period.

examples.en: The fictional report compares purchase frequency across two groups buying sketch paper over the same stated period.
examples.zh: 虚构报告比较两组人在同一指定时段内购买素描纸的「购买频率」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes purchase frequency from how many items the fictional buyers purchased on each shopping trip.
examples.zh: 练习单把「购买频率」与虚构买家每次购物购买的物品数量分开。

words.enDefinition: The stated or inferred likelihood that someone with prior purchase experience will buy the offering again.

examples.en: The fictional survey measures repurchase intention among participants who previously bought an item for the studio.
examples.zh: 虚构调查在以前为工作室购买过该物品的参与者中测量「再次购买意向」。

examples.en: Our class contrasts repurchase intention with a recorded second purchase in the fictional research results table.
examples.zh: 全班将「再次购买意向」与虚构研究结果表中记录的第二次购买作比较。

words.enDefinition: A spontaneous purchase made under an immediate urge and typically with little prior deliberation.

examples.en: The casebook illustrates an impulse purchase when a fictional shopper suddenly feels like getting a new notebook.
examples.zh: 案例教材用虚构购物者突然想买一本新笔记本的场景说明「冲动购买」。

examples.en: Our seminar asks which part of the story suggests the purchase was an impulse purchase in this case.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，故事哪一部分提示本次购买属于「冲动购买」。

words.enDefinition: A purchase not intended before a particular shopping visit or decision context.

examples.en: The fictional shopper notices a needed item missing from the list and makes an unplanned purchase.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者注意到清单漏掉了一件需要的用品，于是发生一次「未计划的购买」。

examples.en: Our session explains how an unplanned purchase can result from remembering an earlier need during shopping.
examples.zh: 课堂说明购物时想起先前需求也会引起「未计划的购买」。

words.enDefinition: A model linking satisfaction to how perceived performance compares with prior expectations.

examples.en: The seminar uses the expectancy disconfirmation model to interpret a fictional student's satisfaction with a recently purchased folder.
examples.zh: 研讨课用「期望不一致模型」解释虚构学生对刚购文件夹的满意程度。

examples.en: Our worksheet applies the expectancy disconfirmation model by comparing fictional reports of expected and experienced product performance.
examples.zh: 练习单比较预期产品表现与实际体验的虚构报告，应用了「期望不一致模型」。

collocations: predictions of the expectancy disconfirmation model

words.enDefinition: In satisfaction research, a comparison in which experienced performance exceeds the consumer's prior expectations.

examples.en: The fictional report illustrates positive disconfirmation when the folder holds more materials than the buyer originally expected.
examples.zh: 虚构报告中文件夹能装下的材料比买家最初预期更多，体现「实际表现超出预期」。

examples.en: Our classroom chart represents positive disconfirmation with a performance rating above the expectation rating in the example.
examples.zh: 课堂图在示例中用高于预期评分的表现评分表示「实际表现超出预期」。

words.enDefinition: In satisfaction research, a comparison in which experienced performance falls short of the consumer's prior expectations.

examples.en: The case illustrates negative disconfirmation when the fictional shopper reports that the box held fewer items than expected.
examples.zh: 案例中，虚构购物者报告盒子容纳的物品少于预想，体现了「实际表现低于预期」。

examples.en: The class distinguishes negative disconfirmation from simply having low expectations before using the product in the example.
examples.zh: 全班区分了「实际表现低于预期」和使用虚构产品前原本就抱有较低期望。

words.enDefinition: Disappointment felt after buying, involving the thought that a different choice might have turned out better.

examples.en: The fictional shopper reports purchase regret after thinking that a different notebook might have suited the assignment better.
examples.zh: 虚构购物者觉得另一款笔记本也许更适合这项作业，于是表示有「购后懊悔」。

examples.en: Our seminar distinguishes purchase regret from dissatisfaction that does not involve comparing the choice with an alternative.
examples.zh: 研讨课区分「购后懊悔」和未将所选方案与其他选项作比较时的不满意。

words.enDefinition: A negative evaluation of how a product or service performed in use or purchase.

examples.en: The fictional survey summary records consumer dissatisfaction with a folder described as difficult to close in class.
examples.zh: 虚构调查摘要记录了因文件夹据说在课堂上不好合上而产生的「消费者不满」。

examples.en: Our discussion compares consumer dissatisfaction with reports of product performance in the same fictional student sample.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论把「消费者不满」与相同虚构学生样本所报告的产品表现作比较。

words.enDefinition: A group of consumers in a broader market who share characteristics, needs, or behaviour relevant to the offering.

examples.en: The case describes a market segment of fictional buyers who mainly need folders for larger drawings.
examples.zh: 案例描述了一个「细分市场群体」，其中的虚构买家主要需要装较大画稿的文件夹。

examples.en: Our worksheet represents a market segment as a group with a shared need within the fictional market.
examples.zh: 练习单用虚构市场中有共同需求的一群人表示一个「细分市场群体」。

words.enDefinition: A characteristic, kind of information, or criterion used to divide a market into distinct groups.

examples.en: The fictional study uses intended use as its segmentation base for grouping buyers of art supplies.
examples.zh: 虚构研究根据预定用途对美术用品买家分组，把它作为「市场细分依据」。

examples.en: Our seminar asks why the same market might yield different groups under a different segmentation base.
examples.zh: 研讨课询问，同一个市场按照不同的「市场细分依据」为什么会形成不同的群体。

collocations: compare a segmentation base with another

words.enDefinition: A description of a market segment's relevant characteristics, needs, and typical buying or use patterns.

examples.en: The students read a segment profile summarising preferences across a fictional group of buyers in the exercise.
examples.zh: 学生阅读了一个「细分群体概貌」，其中概括了练习里一个虚构买家群体的偏好。

examples.en: Our class compares two versions of a segment profile based on different summaries of the same fictional survey.
examples.zh: 全班比较了基于同一虚构调查的不同摘要写成的两份「细分群体概貌」。

words.enDefinition: Dividing a market into groups by places or geographic conditions relevant to the market.

examples.en: The fictional report uses geographic segmentation to describe demand in several broad regions with different climates.
examples.zh: 虚构报告用「地理细分」描述几个气候不同的大区的需求。

examples.en: Our class compares geographic segmentation with grouping fictional consumers by the product benefits they seek instead.
examples.zh: 全班把「地理细分」和按虚构消费者希望获得的产品利益分组作比较。

words.enDefinition: Dividing a market by relevant population characteristics described in demographic categories.

examples.en: The teaching example illustrates demographic segmentation using aggregated counts for broad categories in a fictional population table.
examples.zh: 教学示例用虚构人口表中宽泛类别的汇总人数说明「人口统计细分」。

examples.en: Our worksheet discusses demographic segmentation separately from grouping consumers by their reasons for choosing a product.
examples.zh: 练习单分别说明「人口统计细分」和按消费者选产品的原因分组。

words.enDefinition: Dividing a market by shared lifestyles, values, interests, or similar characteristics rather than solely by demographics.

examples.en: The course illustrates psychographic segmentation with fictional profiles that differ in their reported leisure interests and activities.
examples.zh: 课程用在自报休闲兴趣与活动上有所不同的虚构画像说明「心理特征细分」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares psychographic segmentation with a classification based only on region in the same fictional example.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「心理特征细分」与在同一虚构示例中仅依据地区作的分类相比。

words.enDefinition: Dividing consumers into groups using similarities in activities, interests, or patterns of daily life.

examples.en: The fictional exercise illustrates lifestyle segmentation by distinguishing groups with different leisure routines in a sample report.
examples.zh: 虚构练习通过区分样本报告中休闲习惯不同的群体，说明「生活方式细分」。

examples.en: Our lecture discusses lifestyle segmentation as one way to interpret the broad descriptions supplied for the fictional market.
examples.zh: 讲座把「生活方式细分」作为解读虚构市场宽泛描述的一种方法。

words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers according to the problems they want solved or the needs they want met.

examples.en: The classroom case uses needs-based segmentation to separate people seeking easier storage from those seeking convenient transport.
examples.zh: 课堂案例用「基于需求的细分」区分想更容易收纳的人和想更方便携带的人。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares needs-based segmentation with a fictional grouping that ignores why consumers want the product.
examples.zh: 练习单把「基于需求的细分」与一个忽略消费者为何想要产品的虚构分组作比较。

words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers by the particular outcomes or advantages they seek from a product category.

examples.en: The sample report uses benefit segmentation to group fictional consumers by portability, durability, or ease of cleaning.
examples.zh: 样本报告对虚构消费者作「按所求利益细分」，分为看重轻便、耐用或便于清洁等不同的小组。

examples.en: Our class compares benefit segmentation with grouping the same fictional consumers by how frequently they use the product.
examples.zh: 全班比较「按所求利益细分」与按照使用频率对同一批虚构消费者分组。

words.enDefinition: Grouping market members by differences in how they purchase, use, or respond to offerings.

examples.en: The fictional research report illustrates behavioral segmentation using published summaries of how frequently a kitchen item is used.
examples.zh: 虚构研究报告用已公布的某厨具使用频率汇总来说明「行为细分」。

examples.en: Our seminar compares behavioral segmentation with a grouping based on the regions shown in the fictional market table.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「行为细分」与按照虚构市场表所示地区分组进行对比。

words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers by the situations or events associated with buying or using a product.

examples.en: The textbook uses occasion segmentation to distinguish purchases for routine studio work from purchases for a fictional exhibition.
examples.zh: 教材用「按场合细分」区分日常工作室使用的采购和为虚构展览所作的采购。

examples.en: Our class asks which fictional groups arise from occasion segmentation in the sample report on storage supplies.
examples.zh: 全班询问，收纳用品样本报告里的哪些虚构群体来自「按场合细分」。

words.enDefinition: A particular event or situation in which a consumer uses a product or service.

examples.en: The fictional diary describes an afternoon studio session as the main usage occasion for the portable folder.
examples.zh: 虚构日记把工作室下午的一次活动描述为便携文件夹的主要「产品使用场合」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes a usage occasion from when the character originally bought the item in the story.
examples.zh: 练习单区分了「产品使用场合」和故事中角色最初购买这件物品的时点。

words.zhGloss: 按使用频率或用量细分
words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers according to how often or how much they use a category of product.
acceptedZhAnswers: 按使用频率或用量细分

examples.en: The class illustrates usage-rate segmentation by reading a fictional table of rare and frequent categories of use.
examples.zh: 全班阅读一张有关低频和高频使用类别的虚构表格，说明「按使用频率或用量细分」。

examples.en: Our textbook separates usage-rate segmentation from grouping people according to which product features they say they prefer.
examples.zh: 教材把「按使用频率或用量细分」与按消费者所说的产品特征偏好进行分组区分开。

words.enDefinition: The frequency or amount of use of a product within a specified period or among a stated group.

examples.en: The sample research report compares product usage rate across three fictional groups during the same stated period.
examples.zh: 研究报告样本比较三个虚构群体在同一规定时段内的「产品使用频率或用量」。

examples.en: Our class asks whether product usage rate in the example refers to number of uses or quantity used.
examples.zh: 全班讨论示例中的「产品使用频率或用量」是指使用次数还是使用数量。

words.enDefinition: A consumer classified at the lower end of product use according to a stated measure or category.

examples.en: The fictional survey labels someone a light user when their reported use falls in the lowest category.
examples.zh: 当某人的自报使用量属于最低档时，虚构调查将其标为「低频或低用量用户」。

examples.en: Our class checks which time period the report uses before interpreting the light user label in the table.
examples.zh: 全班先核对报告所用时间段，再理解表中的「低频或低用量用户」标签。

collocations: behaviour reported by a light user

words.enDefinition: A consumer classified at the upper end of product use according to a stated measure or category.

examples.en: The fictional study classifies a participant as a heavy user based on reported frequency within the month.
examples.zh: 虚构研究根据参与者报告的月内使用频率，将一人归为「高频或高用量用户」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether the same heavy user threshold applies to both products in the fictional chart.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构图表中的两种产品是否采用相同的「高频或高用量用户」阈值。

collocations: responses attributed to a heavy user

words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers by whether they are nonusers, first-time users, regular users, or at another stage of use.

examples.en: The fictional dataset uses user status segmentation to distinguish people who have tried a product from nonusers.
examples.zh: 虚构数据集用「按用户使用状态细分」来区分试过产品的人和没有使用的人。

examples.en: Our class compares user status segmentation with a method that only counts frequency among current fictional users.
examples.zh: 全班把「按用户使用状态细分」与仅统计虚构当前用户频次的方法作比较。

words.enDefinition: Someone who does not use products in the category under study during the relevant reference period.

examples.en: The fictional questionnaire identifies a category nonuser without asking about purchases of any particular product or brand.
examples.zh: 虚构问卷辨认「某品类的非使用者」，无须询问任何特定产品或品牌的购买情况。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether a category nonuser is included in the denominator of the displayed aggregate table.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，所展示汇总表的分母是否包括「某品类的非使用者」。

words.enDefinition: Someone using the product or category for the first time, as defined in the study.

examples.en: The fictional survey labels someone a first-time user based on whether they had used the product before.
examples.zh: 虚构调查根据某人过去是否使用过该产品，把参与者标为「首次使用者」。

examples.en: Our class analyses the first-time user category separately from people who report past use in the fictional chart.
examples.zh: 全班把「首次使用者」类别与虚构图表中报告过往用过产品的人分别分析。

words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers by how consistently they prefer or buy one offering relative to alternatives, as defined in the study.

examples.en: The seminar introduces loyalty status segmentation by comparing aggregate fictional patterns of repeat purchase across different products.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较不同产品的虚构复购汇总模式，以介绍「按忠诚状态细分」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks how loyalty status segmentation differs from counting how often fictional buyers purchase the category overall.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「按忠诚状态细分」与统计虚构买家购买整个品类的频次有何差别。

words.enDefinition: The estimated count or proportion of consumers belonging to a market segment.

examples.en: The fictional market report gives segment size as both a count and a percentage of all buyers.
examples.zh: 虚构市场报告用人数和占所有买家的百分比两种方式表示「细分群体规模」。

examples.en: Our class compares segment size across two estimates that use different reference populations for the fictional example.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构示例中使用不同基准总体的两个估计所给出的「细分群体规模」。

words.enDefinition: The possibility that a market segment will grow in size, demand, or economic value over time.

examples.en: Our casebook compares segment growth potential using two alternative sets of assumptions about the fictional market outlook.
examples.zh: 案例教材采用两套关于虚构市场前景的假设来比较「细分群体增长潜力」。

examples.en: The classroom report discusses segment growth potential separately from the current size of the fictional buyer population.
examples.zh: 课堂报告将「细分群体增长潜力」与虚构买家总体的当前规模分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which serving a segment can generate profit under specified revenue, cost, and other assumptions.

examples.en: The fictional report discusses segment profitability by presenting estimated revenue and estimated costs in adjacent table columns.
examples.zh: 虚构报告相邻两列分别给出预计收入和预计成本，用以讨论「细分群体盈利性」。

examples.en: Our seminar separates segment profitability from the larger number of customers described in one of the fictional profiles.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「细分群体盈利性」与虚构画像之一所描述的较大客户人数分开。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a segment's size and relevant characteristics can be estimated with available evidence.

examples.en: The textbook illustrates segment measurability by comparing classes with published aggregate counts and classes without adequate counts.
examples.zh: 教材比较有已公布汇总人数的类别和缺乏足够统计的类别，用来说明「细分群体可衡量性」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which part of the fictional summary provides evidence about segment measurability in the example.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，虚构摘要的哪一部分为示例中的「细分群体可衡量性」提供依据。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a business can reach and serve members of a market segment under stated conditions.

examples.en: The seminar assesses segment accessibility using the delivery areas described in a fictional supplier's public service summary.
examples.zh: 研讨课依据虚构供应商公开服务摘要中描述的配送地区评估「细分群体可触达性」。

examples.en: Our class discusses segment accessibility separately from the potential size of the audience in the fictional market.
examples.zh: 全班将「细分群体可触达性」与虚构市场中的潜在受众规模分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: The degree to which a segment is sufficiently large or valuable to justify serving it under stated conditions.

examples.en: The class discusses segment substantiality by comparing the fictional groups with the costs described in the example.
examples.zh: 全班把示例描述的成本与虚构群体对照，用来讨论「细分群体规模充足性」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes segment substantiality from the practical ability to deliver the offering to the fictional users.
examples.zh: 练习单将「细分群体规模充足性」与实际能否向虚构用户交付产品分开。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which a market segment can be meaningfully distinguished from others in relevant needs or responses.

examples.en: The fictional report illustrates segment differentiability by comparing groups whose members value different outcomes from the same product.
examples.zh: 虚构报告比较重视同一产品不同使用结果的群体，说明「细分群体可区分性」。

examples.en: Our class compares reactions across the fictional groups to see whether there is evidence of segment differentiability.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构群体之间的反应，看看能否找到有关「细分群体可区分性」的证据。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which available resources and capabilities can support practical offerings or plans for a segment.

examples.en: The case discusses segment actionability by comparing the imagined supplier's capabilities with the stated needs of the group.
examples.zh: 案例将想象中供应商的能力与群体所述需求对照，用来讨论「细分群体可实施性」。

examples.en: Our seminar examines why segment actionability may differ even between two similarly sized fictional groups of consumers.
examples.zh: 研讨课探讨，即使两个虚构消费者群体规模相近，「细分群体可实施性」为何也可能不同。

words.zhGloss: 细分群体内部的相似性
words.enDefinition: The degree to which members of the same market segment share characteristics relevant to the segmentation.
acceptedZhAnswers: 细分群体内部的相似性

examples.en: The fictional results illustrate within-segment similarity when most members of one group report the same practical need.
examples.zh: 虚构结果中，同一组的大多数成员报告相同实际需求，用以说明「细分群体内部的相似性」。

examples.en: Our class compares within-segment similarity across two alternative ways of grouping the fictional survey responses in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 全班比较练习单中用两种不同方式对虚构问卷回答分组所表现出的「细分群体内部的相似性」。

words.enDefinition: Differences in relevant needs, characteristics, or behaviours between distinct market segments.

examples.en: The class examines between-segment differences in fictional responses about storage space and the intended use of the product.
examples.zh: 全班分析关于储存空间和产品预定用途的虚构答复里呈现的「细分群体之间的差异」。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which between-segment differences matter when interpreting the broad profiles given for the fictional example.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，在解读虚构示例中的概略画像时，哪些「细分群体之间的差异」有意义。

words.enDefinition: A situation where two market segments share some members or features under the criteria used.

examples.en: The example shows segment overlap when some fictional respondents meet the criteria for two groups in the table.
examples.zh: 示例显示，部分虚构应答者同时符合表中两个群体的标准，因而出现「细分群体重叠」。

examples.en: Our class notes segment overlap before combining the counts listed for the fictional project in two categories.
examples.zh: 全班先留意「细分群体重叠」，再合并虚构项目归入两个类别的人数。

words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers by life transitions or roles that may be associated with different needs.

examples.en: The textbook illustrates life-stage segmentation by comparing fictional buyers preparing for independent living with buyers replacing familiar items.
examples.zh: 教材比较准备独立生活的虚构买家和更换熟悉物品的虚构买家，用以说明「按生活阶段细分」。

examples.en: Our class discusses life-stage segmentation using broad descriptions of transitions rather than information about actual individuals.
examples.zh: 课堂根据对生活转折的概括性描述讨论「按生活阶段细分」，没有使用真实个人资料。

words.enDefinition: Grouping consumers by shared attitudes toward an offering, category, or market issue.

examples.en: The synthetic survey uses attitudinal segmentation to summarise fictional respondents' views about sharing studio supplies.
examples.zh: 合成调查使用「按态度细分」概括虚构应答者对共用工作室用品的看法。

examples.en: Our worksheet contrasts attitudinal segmentation with a grouping based entirely on recorded product use in the fictional material.
examples.zh: 练习单将「按态度细分」与完全按照虚构材料里记载的产品使用情况分组作对比。

words.enDefinition: Systematic inquiry into a market, including consumers' needs, demand, competing offerings, or relevant market conditions.

examples.en: The introductory class uses market research to explain how a fictional survey can inform understanding of product demand.
examples.zh: 入门课借「市场调研」说明虚构调查怎样帮助了解产品需求。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares two findings from market research about the same fictional market for studio supplies.
examples.zh: 练习单比较了关于同一个虚构工作室用品市场的两项「市场调研」发现。

words.enDefinition: A document setting out why a market study is needed, the questions it should address, and its expected outputs.

examples.en: The fictional market research brief lists the decision context and questions before describing the expected report.
examples.zh: 虚构「市场调研任务简报」先列出决策背景和问题，再描述预期报告。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the final summary answers the questions in the market research brief for the exercise.
examples.zh: 全班核对，最终摘要是否回答练习所给「市场调研任务简报」里的问题。

collocations: requirements in a market research brief

words.enDefinition: An information gap or question that a marketing study is intended to address.

examples.en: The fictional client asks whether folder sizes meet the needs of students, which defines the marketing research problem.
examples.zh: 虚构委托方询问文件夹尺寸是否符合学生需要，由此明确「营销调研问题」。

examples.en: Our seminar separates the marketing research problem from the practical choice the fictional client eventually needs to make.
examples.zh: 研讨课区分了「营销调研问题」与虚构委托方最终需要作出的实际选择。

words.enDefinition: The practical choice a manager needs to make and for which research may supply information.

examples.en: The fictional supplier's management decision problem is whether to offer another size of storage box next term.
examples.zh: 虚构供应商的「管理决策问题」是下一学期是否再提供一种尺寸的储物盒。

examples.en: Our class converts a management decision problem into questions about what the fictional consumers need from the product.
examples.zh: 全班把一项「管理决策问题」转化为关于虚构消费者需要该产品提供什么的问题。

words.enDefinition: A specified piece of knowledge, comparison, or estimate that a market study aims to produce.

examples.en: The fictional brief states one market research objective as estimating the share of respondents seeking a lighter product.
examples.zh: 虚构简报将估计希望产品更轻的回答者所占比例列为一项「市场调研目标」。

examples.en: Our tutor asks which market research objective can be answered with the information shown in the sample table.
examples.zh: 老师询问，样本表显示的信息能满足哪项「市场调研目标」。

words.enDefinition: A plan connecting market research questions with the sources, study methods, analysis, and reporting to be used.

examples.en: The classroom market research plan names the information sources that two groups will compare in the fictional study.
examples.zh: 课堂「市场调研计划」列出了两个小组在虚构研究中将比较的信息来源。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether the market research plan matches the information needs stated in the fictional brief.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「市场调研计划」是否符合虚构简报提出的信息需求。

collocations: requirements of a market research plan

words.enDefinition: A person or organisation that requests and usually funds a study carried out by a research provider.

examples.en: The role chart identifies the research commissioner as the fictional organisation asking for the market study.
examples.zh: 角色图将要求进行市场研究的虚构机构列为「调研委托方」。

examples.en: Our class asks how the research commissioner expressed the decision context in the fictional briefing document.
examples.zh: 全班询问，「调研委托方」在虚构任务说明中怎样表述决策背景。

words.enDefinition: A business or organisation providing market research services or data to a client.

examples.en: Our fictional proposal identifies the market research supplier responsible for preparing the final aggregate report on consumer preferences.
examples.zh: 虚构提案列明负责编制消费者偏好最终汇总报告的「市场调研服务机构」。

examples.en: The worksheet distinguishes the market research supplier from the organisation that commissioned the study in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习单将「市场调研服务机构」与练习中委托研究的机构区分开。

collocations: work with a market research supplier
report from a market research supplier

words.enDefinition: Research designed for a particular client's questions and information needs.

examples.en: The exercise contrasts custom market research for one fictional supplier with a report available to many subscribers.
examples.zh: 练习把对某个虚构供应商的「定制市场调研」与可供许多订阅者获取的报告相对照。

examples.en: Our case uses custom market research to answer questions unique to the fictional campus shop's product category.
examples.zh: 案例用「定制市场调研」回答虚构校园商店这一产品品类特有的问题。

words.zhGloss: 多客户共享的标准化调研
words.enDefinition: Research designed and produced by a provider for multiple clients who receive access to common findings or data.
acceptedZhAnswers: 多客户共享的标准化调研

examples.en: The class reads a simulated syndicated research summary that several fictional clients can access for the same category.
examples.zh: 全班阅读一个「多客户共享的标准化调研」的模拟摘要，多个虚构客户可查阅该品类的这一摘要。

examples.en: Our class compares syndicated research and custom research when reviewing the two sample proposals for a study.
examples.zh: 全班审阅两份调研样本提案时，比较了「多客户共享的标准化调研」和定制调研。

words.enDefinition: A survey combining separate sets of questions commissioned by different clients in one shared study.

examples.en: The fictional omnibus survey contains separate sections on storage products and food containers for two different clients.
examples.zh: 虚构「多客户合用问卷调查」包含两个分别给不同客户的板块，涉及储物产品和食品容器。

examples.en: Our tutor describes an omnibus survey as a shared vehicle for unrelated questions in the sample proposal.
examples.zh: 老师将「多客户合用问卷调查」描述为样本提案中承载互不相关问题的共同渠道。

collocations: include questions in an omnibus survey

words.enDefinition: A group of people who have agreed to be invited to take part in consumer research studies over time.

examples.en: The fictional research provider describes a consumer research panel whose members can choose whether to answer each survey.
examples.zh: 虚构调研机构介绍了一个「消费者调研样本库」，成员可选择是否参加每次调查。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes a consumer research panel from the subset of fictional members who joined one particular study.
examples.zh: 练习单区分「消费者调研样本库」和参加某次具体研究的虚构成员子集。

collocations: sample from a consumer research panel
voluntary participation in a consumer research panel

words.enDefinition: A column in a survey cross-tabulation that reports results for one specified respondent group.

examples.en: The banner point for weekly visitors displayed responses from that group across all the selected questions.
examples.zh: 每道选定问题里，周访客这一「交叉表中的分组列」都显示该组的回答。

examples.en: We checked the sample size for each banner point before comparing percentages across the columns.
examples.zh: 比较各列百分比前，我们先检查「交叉表中的分组列」各自的样本量。

collocations: base size for a banner point

words.enDefinition: In market research, the proportion of screened people who satisfy a study's stated eligibility criteria.

examples.en: The synthetic table reports the incidence rate in market research using the qualified group and the number screened.
examples.zh: 合成表根据符合条件者的人数和接受筛选的人数报告「市场调研资格符合率」。

examples.en: Our class checks the denominator before interpreting the incidence rate in market research in the fictional survey summary.
examples.zh: 全班先核对分母，再解读虚构调查摘要中的「市场调研资格符合率」。

collocations: report the incidence rate in market research
compare the incidence rate in market research
denominator of the incidence rate in market research

words.enDefinition: Research that examines both how consumers use a product category and how they evaluate it or its offerings.

examples.en: The fictional usage and attitude study combines reported use frequency with opinions about a category of containers.
examples.zh: 虚构的「使用与态度调研」将报告的使用频次与对某类容器的看法结合起来。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which questions in the usage and attitude study describe behaviour and which describe attitudes.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，「使用与态度调研」中哪些问题描述行为，哪些描述态度。

collocations: conduct a usage and attitude study
findings from a usage and attitude study
design of a usage and attitude study

words.enDefinition: Research focusing on how, when, or how often people use products or services in a category.

examples.en: The casebook summarises a category usage study about how fictional students use different kinds of studio storage.
examples.zh: 案例教材概述了一项「品类使用调研」，内容是虚构学生怎样使用不同类型的工作室收纳用品。

examples.en: Our class compares the category usage study with the later survey about how fictional buyers evaluate new options.
examples.zh: 全班把「品类使用调研」与之后关于虚构买家如何评价新选项的调查作比较。

collocations: findings of a category usage study
scope of a category usage study

words.enDefinition: A concept test in which each participant evaluates one concept, with any comparisons made across separate groups.

examples.en: The class reads a fictional monadic concept test report where each group assessed only one product idea.
examples.zh: 全班阅读一份虚构「单概念独立测评」报告，其中各小组只评价一项产品构想。

examples.en: Our tutor asks why a monadic concept test does not contain within-person comparisons of the two fictional concepts.
examples.zh: 老师询问，为什么「单概念独立测评」不包含同一个人对两项虚构概念作出的对比。

collocations: results of a monadic concept test
compare a monadic concept test with another format

words.enDefinition: A test in which a participant evaluates several concepts or products one at a time, rating each separately.

examples.en: The classroom summary describes a sequential monadic test with separate ratings of each fictional product idea in order.
examples.zh: 课堂摘要描述了一项「顺序独立测评」，按次序分别给每个虚构产品构想评分。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks whether earlier items might affect scores later in a fictional sequential monadic test report.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，在虚构「顺序独立测评」报告中，先出现的项目是否可能影响后面的评分。

collocations: results of a sequential monadic test
order effects in a sequential monadic test

words.enDefinition: A test asking participants to compare two presented options directly according to a stated criterion.

examples.en: The fictional paired comparison test reports how many people preferred one folder over the other for portability.
examples.zh: 虚构「成对比较测试」报告了有多少人从便携性出发更喜欢其中一个文件夹。

examples.en: Our seminar distinguishes a paired comparison test from separate ratings of unrelated ideas in the other example.
examples.zh: 研讨课区分了「成对比较测试」与另一示例中对彼此无关的构想分别打分的做法。

collocations: results of a paired comparison test
criterion in a paired comparison test

words.enDefinition: A reference product idea used as a standard when comparing responses to another idea.

examples.en: The fictional benchmark concept gives the class a reference point for interpreting ratings of the new folder idea.
examples.zh: 虚构「对照概念」给全班提供了参照点，以解读新文件夹构想的评分。

examples.en: Our worksheet asks which rating in the sample table belongs to the benchmark concept provided for comparison.
examples.zh: 练习单询问，样本表哪一项评分对应供比较的「对照概念」。

collocations: compare ratings with a benchmark concept

words.enDefinition: How attractive or interesting potential consumers find a proposed product idea under the stated evaluation conditions.

examples.en: The fictional results compare concept appeal for two proposed containers using the same question and response scale.
examples.zh: 虚构结果采用同一问题和回答量表，比较两款拟议容器的「产品概念吸引力」。

examples.en: Our class discusses concept appeal separately from the feasibility of making the fictional item on campus.
examples.zh: 全班将「产品概念吸引力」与在校园制作该虚构物品的可行性分开讨论。

words.enDefinition: The extent to which respondents see a proposed product idea as different from alternatives they know.

examples.en: The fictional concept report presents perceived concept uniqueness alongside a separate measure of how attractive each idea seems.
examples.zh: 虚构概念报告将「感知产品概念独特性」与对各构想吸引力的单独衡量并排列出。

examples.en: Our class discusses whether perceived concept uniqueness can differ by familiarity with the category in the fictional study.
examples.zh: 全班讨论在虚构研究中，「感知产品概念独特性」是否会因品类熟悉程度而异。

words.enDefinition: A product test in which consenting participants try an item in their everyday home setting and report their experience.

examples.en: The fictional in-home use test summary describes aggregate experiences with a storage item used in ordinary households.
examples.zh: 虚构的「居家使用测试」摘要描述了普通家庭使用一款收纳用品的汇总体验。

examples.en: Our worksheet compares an in-home use test with evaluations carried out in a single classroom location.
examples.zh: 练习单将「居家使用测试」与在一个课堂地点进行的评价作比较。

collocations: results of an in-home use test
product evaluated in an in-home use test
report from an in-home use test

words.enDefinition: A product or concept evaluation held at a common research location under broadly similar conditions for participants.

examples.en: The classroom chart describes a central location test where fictional participants evaluated sample folders at the same venue.
examples.zh: 课堂图表描述一项「集中场地测试」，虚构参与者在同一地点评价文件夹样品。

examples.en: Our tutor contrasts the central location test summary with the separate report about use in typical household settings.
examples.zh: 老师把「集中场地测试」摘要与关于典型家庭使用场景的另一份报告作比较。

collocations: findings of a central location test
conditions in a central location test

words.enDefinition: A direct quotation from a consumer's response used to illustrate a point in a research report or presentation.

examples.en: The fictional report labels a consumer verbatim beside the aggregate finding it is intended to illustrate in class.
examples.zh: 虚构报告把一则「消费者原话摘录」标在它准备于课堂说明的汇总发现旁。

examples.en: Our tutor asks whether the consumer verbatim illustrates the finding or represents the entire group of fictional respondents.
examples.zh: 老师询问，「消费者原话摘录」是用于说明这一发现，还是能代表全部虚构应答者。

words.enDefinition: The number or set of respondents whose answers are included in a reported survey calculation.

examples.en: The fictional chart specifies the respondent base below each percentage to show who is included in the calculation.
examples.zh: 虚构图在各百分比下方注明「受访者计算基数」，说明计算时涉及哪些人。

examples.en: Our worksheet shows that the respondent base changes when only fictional users answer the question about product use.
examples.zh: 练习单显示，只让虚构用户回答产品使用问题时，「受访者计算基数」会变化。

collocations: percentage calculated on a respondent base

words.enDefinition: The percentage of respondents selecting the single highest response category on a rating scale.

examples.en: The fictional table reports a top-box score using only the highest response category in the exercise.
examples.zh: 虚构表仅用练习中最高回答档计算「最高档回答占比」。

examples.en: Our seminar checks the respondent base before comparing the top-box score across two fictional product ideas.
examples.zh: 研讨课先核对受访者计算基数，再比较两项虚构产品构想的「最高档回答占比」。

words.zhGloss: 最高两档回答合计占比
words.enDefinition: The percentage of respondents whose ratings fall in either of the two highest categories on a scale.
acceptedZhAnswers: 最高两档回答合计占比

examples.en: The fictional report combines the highest two categories to calculate the top-two-box score for one proposal.
examples.zh: 虚构报告合并最高的两个类别，计算其中一项提案的「最高两档回答合计占比」。

examples.en: Our class compares the top-two-box score with the share giving only the single highest rating in the table.
examples.zh: 全班将「最高两档回答合计占比」与表中只给出最高分的比例相比较。

words.enDefinition: The percentage of respondents selecting the single lowest response category on a rating scale.

examples.en: The fictional summary includes a bottom-box score next to the distribution of all ratings for the product concept.
examples.zh: 虚构摘要将「最低档回答占比」列在产品概念全部评分的分布旁。

examples.en: Our class checks the scale labels before interpreting the bottom-box score in the sample survey report.
examples.zh: 全班先查看量表标签，再解读调查报告样本里的「最低档回答占比」。

words.enDefinition: An evidence-informed understanding of a consumer need, motive, or pattern that helps explain observed choices or attitudes.

examples.en: The class develops a consumer insight by comparing why fictional shoppers chose similar items for different reasons.
examples.zh: 全班比较虚构购物者为何出于不同原因挑选相似物品，据此形成一项「消费者洞察」。

examples.en: Our worksheet distinguishes a consumer insight from a single raw percentage in the sample study's summary table.
examples.zh: 练习单把「消费者洞察」与研究样本汇总表里的单一原始百分比分开。

words.enDefinition: A short statement expressing a meaningful interpretation of research evidence about a customer or market issue.

examples.en: The tutor asks for an insight statement that explains why the two fictional groups favour different product features.
examples.zh: 老师要求写出一条「洞察陈述」，解释两个虚构群体为何偏好不同的产品特征。

examples.en: Our class checks whether the insight statement is supported by the aggregate results in the fictional report.
examples.zh: 全班核对，虚构报告的汇总结果能否支持这条「洞察陈述」。

words.enDefinition: A concise description of the outcome or practical problem a consumer needs addressed, usually independent of any proposed solution.

examples.en: The fictional brief includes a consumer need statement about keeping large papers flat during travel to class.
examples.zh: 虚构简报给出一条「消费者需求陈述」，内容是在去上课的路上使大幅纸张保持平整。

examples.en: Our class compares the consumer need statement with a later proposal naming one specific design for a folder.
examples.zh: 全班把「消费者需求陈述」与后来指出文件夹某种具体设计的提案作比较。

collocations: support a consumer need statement with evidence

words.enDefinition: A discussion or presentation after a study that summarises findings, explains limitations, and connects them to the study questions.

examples.en: The fictional research team presents its market research debrief after analysing the results from two product evaluations.
examples.zh: 虚构调研团队分析完两项产品评价的结果后，进行「市场调研结果汇报」。

examples.en: Our class asks whether the market research debrief provides enough context to interpret the ratings in the example.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，「市场调研结果汇报」提供的背景是否足以帮助解读示例中的评分。

collocations: findings in a market research debrief

words.zhGloss: 可用于采取行动的洞察
words.enDefinition: An evidence-supported interpretation with clear relevance to a decision or next step.
acceptedZhAnswers: 可用于采取行动的洞察

examples.en: The class calls the comparison an actionable insight because it informs the fictional team's choice between two prototypes.
examples.zh: 全班把这项比较称为「可用于采取行动的洞察」，因为它有助于虚构团队在两种原型间作选择。

examples.en: Our tutor asks whether the actionable insight addresses the question originally stated in the fictional research brief.
examples.zh: 老师询问，「可用于采取行动的洞察」是否回应了虚构调研简报最初提出的问题。
